missed_core_items.description: The paper includes a theoretical analysis (Theorem 1) showing that DropEdge either increases the relaxed smoothing layer or reduces information loss, which is a core contribution.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Theorem 1. We denote the original graph as G and the one after dropping certain edges out as G′. Given a small value of ϵ, we assume G and G′ will encounter the ϵ-smoothing issue with regard to subspaces M and M′, respectively. Then, either of the following inequalities holds after sufficient edges removed. • The relaxed smoothing layer only increases: ˆl(M, ϵ) ≤ ˆl(M′, ϵ); • The information loss is decreased: N − dim(M) > N − dim(M′).

missed_core_items.description: The paper reports that DropEdge reduces validation loss on multiple backbones, indicating alleviation of over-fitting, as shown in Figure 2b and Figure 6.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: In addition, the validation losses of all 4-layer models on Cora are shown in Figure 2b. The curves along the training epoch are dramatically pulled down after applying DropEdge, which also explains the effect of DropEdge on alleviating over-fitting.

missed_core_items.description: The paper demonstrates that DropEdge slows down over-smoothing by showing higher distance between layer outputs and slower convergence, as in Figure 3.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Conversely, the model with DropEdge (p = 0.8) reveals higher distance and slower convergent speed than that without DropEdge (p = 0), implying the importance of DropEdge to alleviating over-smoothing.

missed_core_items.description: The paper shows that DropEdge is compatible with Dropout, and using both further decreases validation loss, as in Figure 4a.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: It reads that while both Dropout and DropEdge are able to facilitate the training of GCN, the improvement by DropEdge is more significant, and if we adopt them concurrently, the loss is decreased further, indicating the compatibility of DropEdge with Dropout.

missed_core_items.description: The paper reports that layer-wise DropEdge achieves lower training loss but comparable validation loss to original DropEdge, as in Figure 4b.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: As observed from Figure 4b, the LW DropEdge achieves lower training loss than the original version, whereas the validation value between two models is comparable.

missed_core_items.description: The paper states that DropEdge saves memory by making the adjacency matrix sparse, as evidenced by 32-layer IncepGCN without DropEdge incurring OOM while with DropEdge it survives.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Another valuable observation in Table 1 is that the 32-layer IncepGCN without DropEdge incurs the Out-Of-Memory (OOM) issue while the model with DropEdge survives, showing the advantage of DropEdge to save memory consuming by making the adjacency matrix sparse.
